LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 9.1.1 DIPHTHONGS, SENTENCE STRESS AND SIGNING IN CONTEXT

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.1: Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 9.1.1 Diphthongs, sentence stress and signing in context
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 9.1.1 Diphthongs, sentence stress and signing in context, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to pronounce words correctly? 2. Why is it important to articulate signs or fingerspell words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signs of vocabulary related to heroes and heroines

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 9.1.1 Diphthongs, sentence stress and signing in context together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication : Learner acquires proper pronunciation or articulation of signing skills as he/she sign read the sentence

while placing stress on different words

Values:
Respect is inculcated during the pronunciation or articulation of signs drills as learners give each other feedback

Link to other subjects

Kiswahili and other languages such as Kenya Sign Language emphasise correct pronunciation or observing proper articulation

of signs of words with correct mouth movement.
